reason: The gap is real. R3 (CONTEXT l.1647-1649) says 'public >= previous stack - 0.001' but never names the reference for K2. The v3 plan (FINAL_REPORT l.190) meant K1 to be the lowrefine comparator. K1 is unscored, and its dummy sha equals the exp57b dummy, so #35 (0.954) is the implied proxy, but that is written nowhere. The probe.json 'rule' is builder boilerplate: tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.2310 stamps 'compare with exp56 ... ties recorded' on every --base x138 build. The choice of reference decides the outcome only when K2 displays 0.952 (a guessed P of ~0.03-0.06). It is still a free rule that should be fixed before K2 scores, and it takes the stricter reference. The timing-confound clause is correct: K2's insertion gate is 8.0 h, the step-0 forecast is <= 7.8 h and L35 was (6.72, 7.73] h, the hidden logs are invisible, and the twin has no insertion, so it is confound-free. One part is wrong. The added 'twin - #34 <= -0.002 ALSO closes lowrefine' as an OR clause should not be adopted. When d2 <= -0.002 the twin is <= 0.951 and already fails the f2 floor (F2 -> exp52). The OR clause's only extra effect is to drop lowrefine from F1 when d1 >= -0.001. That forces a swap from a scored K2 to an unscored K1 (a new submit plus an OK), triggered by a second read on the same embryo, which doubles the rounding risk of a false close (a true -0.0011 can display as -0.002). It also contradicts R3S-1 in the same round ('d2 alone never drops lowrefine'). PC3-01 and R3S-1 are duplicates and should be merged.
fix: Write into CONTEXT before any K2 score (K2 submit 00:01 UTC; earliest score ~06:00), timestamped, as a clarification (the stricter reading, so no OK is needed): 'R3 REFERENCE FOR K2 (pre-score): d1 = K2 - #35 (0.954). #35 is the scored proxy for K1, since the K1 dummy sha == the exp57b dummy and C01 is inert unless a deadline fires. d1 is attributed to lowrefine. d1 >= -0.001: keep lowrefine. d1 <= -0.002 AND L(K2) upper bound <= 8.0 h: drop lowrefine (the R3 removal; the K1 path is per PC3-02/R3S-1 and its submit needs an OK). d1 <= -0.002 AND L(K2) upper bound > 8.0 h: timing confound (the insertion gate may have fired on late hidden clips), not lowrefine harm by itself. Then d2 = twin - #34 (0.953, confound-free) is the lowrefine read: d2 <= -0.002 drops lowrefine, d2 >= -0.001 keeps it. Outside that case, d2 never drops lowrefine; it acts only through the f2 floor. The probe.json rule line (compare with exp56 / ties recorded) is builder boilerplate from build_probe_kernel.py l.2310 and is not a decision rule.' Merge with R3S-1 into one CONTEXT block.
